text:
incident-bot: Pager: P1 - spike in ELB 5xxs and target group failures in eu-west-2 (azd). Affected services: inference-proxy, inference-serving. Alert: ELB_5xx_rate > 10% for 5m. Link: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/alerts/elb-5xx

serena (oncall-sre): I'm on it. I see a big jump in TargetGroup UnhealthyHostCount for tg-inference-eu-west-2a. Latency +5s for new requests.

mike (infra): Observed NAT GW SNAT metrics spike in azd: SNATErrorCount and ConnectionFailures. Also seeing EBS io timeout messages on a subset of instances in the same AZ. EC2 status checks flapping on 3/12 hosts.

irene (oncall-eng): Customer-impact: Support reported several customers getting model timeouts and 502/504 failures. Support ticketID: #12345. We're seeing retries and user-visible latency.

serena (oncall-sre): Reproducing a failing request from inside the VPC (eu-west-2 azd).
```
$ curl -v http://10.0.12.45:8080/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"test"}'
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to 10.0.12.45 (10.0.12.45) port 8080 (#0)
> POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: 10.0.12.45:8080
> Content-Type: application/json
> Content-Length: 16

< HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Time-out
< Server: envoy
< Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2026 02:16:22 GMT
< Content-Length: 0
```

mike (infra): Running tcpdump on one failing instance shows SYN -> SYN-ACK ok but replies to client IP go via natgw-2 while source used natgw-1. Asymmetric routing suspected. Here's a trimmed tcpdump (client->svc):
```
12:34:21.123456 IP 10.0.1.101.49986 > 3.120.45.10.443: Flags [S], seq 0
12:34:21.123789 IP 3.120.45.10.443 > 10.0.1.101.49986: Flags [S.], seq 0
# reply appears from a different public IP (natgw-2) instead of natgw-1
```

serena (oncall-sre): That matches the ELB logs — connections from same client IP are arriving at multiple public IPs tied to different NATs. Could be AZ routing table propagation or an AWS control plane issue.

irene (oncall-eng): EBS errors from dmesg on host: "blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 123456" and kernel showing flush/retry. Might be correlated to the network flap on the host's AZ.

mike (infra): Mitigation options:
- Option A: Shift production traffic away from eu-west-2 azd by adjusting Route53 weights to favor eu-west-1/eu-west-2b.
- Option B: Drain and detach targets in azd from the ELB (force 0 weight / deregister) to stop unhealthy hosts receiving new connections.
- Option C: Engage AWS support/TAM for AZ fabric/networking.

serena (oncall-sre): Starting weighted traffic move now. I'll reduce eu-west-2 (all AZs) weight to 10% and increase eu-west-1 to 90% for inference.redwood.ai using Route53 weighted record set. Executing change.

irene (oncall-eng): Command used (run by infra):
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z123ABC --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"inference.redwood.ai","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"eu-west-1","Weight":900,"TTL":60,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"54.12.34.56"}]} ,{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"inference.redwood.ai","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"eu-west-2","Weight":100,"TTL":60,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"3.120.45.10"}]}}]}'
```

serena (oncall-sre): Also updated elb target group deregistration delay to 30s and enabled connection draining on tg-inference-eu-west-2 to speed failover. Starting to drain the 12 flagged instances.

mike (infra): Opening AWS Support Case: case 987654321 - "Asymmetric public egress path between NAT gateways in eu-west-2 causing ELB target connectivity and EBS IO timeouts". Attached tcpdump, ELB logs, CloudWatch metrics. TAM pinged.

incident-bot: Incident P1 - updated. Timeline entry added: Route53 weights adjusted, ELB draining initiated, AWS Support case opened.

irene (oncall-eng): Early telemetry post-weight-change: 5xx rate dropped from 12% -> 4% in 5m, tail latency improved ~800ms. Some clients still hitting the remaining 10% -> we should keep draining until we confirm stable.

mike (infra): For completeness, I'm also adding a temporary NAT gateway failover: migrating some elastic IPs to natgw-warm in eu-west-1 for outgoing paths so replies are consistent. This is a stopgap.

serena (oncall-sre): Customer communications: @support please update ticket #12345 and post outage advisory: ETA for full recovery unknown, mitigation in-progress (traffic shift + draining).

support (channel): Acknowledged. Drafting a short message to impacted customers and will link to status.redwood.ai.

aws-support-bot: AWS Support: case 987654321 updated - "We see control plane routing entries re-propagating in eu-west-2; engineering is investigating internal NAT route churn. Recommend keeping traffic shifted and we will provide remediation ETA."

serena (oncall-sre): OK. After the weights move and draining we saw healthy recovery in eu-west-2b but azd still noisy. Keeping 10% for now.

irene (oncall-eng): I'm going to collect stable repro logs and create an eval run to monitor model correctness during this degradation window. Will add regression keys to Optimize so we can detect any quality drift.

serena (oncall-sre): Handoff: I'll be handing incident to alex (night-oncall) in 15m. Summary: P1 active, Route53 weights set (eu-west-1=90, eu-west-2=10), ELB targets in azd draining, AWS case open 987654321, customer advisory posted. Current customer-impact reduced but not fully recovered.

alex (night-oncall): Ack taking over. My first actions: monitor CloudWatch for new SNAT errors, confirm AWS reply, keep Route53 weights until AWS confirms fix. Will escalate to SRE lead if any regression > 5% 5xx in next 30m.

incident-bot: Note - last update 4332110450. Assigned: alex (night-oncall).

alex (night-oncall): Short summary for my handoff notes: root suspected: AZ control-plane routing re-propagation causing asymmetric NAT egress; symptom set: ELB 5xx spike, EBS IO timeouts on hosts in azd, customer-facing timeouts. Actions in-flight: Route53 weight shift, ELB drain, AWS case. Next: watch for AWS root cause, consider full failover to eu-west-1 if 5xxs climb back over threshold.
